lines.trans: Are the two of them filming alone again today? Are they even actually shooting?
Is she supposed to be Kuroki's replacement? No way she can replace her.
Yesterday while I was out shopping, I bumped into an old coworker by chance.
From when you worked at the cosmetics counter?
Yes. She already knew that I had appeared in adult videos.
No matter what anyone says, there's no need to let it bother you.

words.gram: Noun in the idiom 気が向く (feel like doing).

lines.trans: It doesn't bother me at all.

lines.trans: I just thought that if I hadn't found your work back then, I'd probably still be working there.
The colorless scenery from the commuter train, and a planner filled with the same routine...
Back then, anything was fine as long as it got me out of there and made me truly free.

meanings.note: Special reading きょう.
Replaces は, が, or を to add 'also' or 'too'.

examples.trans: Please give me this one too.

examples.text: あそこも新しい店です。
examples.trans: Over there is a new shop too.

meanings.note: Native counter reading ふたり; shops politely say お二人様 for 'party of two'.

examples.trans: The two of us go together.

meanings.en: come; go do something and return (after て-form)
meanings.note: Written in kana after a て-form (話してきます), expresses stepping away to do an action and coming back.

examples.text: ちょっと水を買ってきます。
examples.trans: I will go buy some water and be right back.

examples.text: お前ら、観光じゃないんだからしっかりしろよ。
examples.trans: Hey, this isn't sightseeing, so pull yourselves together.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: location of action; means; scope total
meanings.note: Marks where an action happens, the unit/scope of a rate or total (十日で, 全部で), or the cause/occasion.

examples.trans: It is one thousand yen in total.

meanings.note: Everyday spoken counterpart of なぜ or どうして.

examples.text: なんで知っているんですか。

meanings.note: Points to something visible farther away from both speaker and listener.

examples.trans: That over there is a school.

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.
All-purpose action verb; turns Sino-Japanese nouns into verbs (融通する, 出店する) and with に means 'decide on' or 'make into'.
Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).
Attached to names of children, close friends, or familiar acquaintances.

examples.text: トシちゃん、また来たの？
その代わり、今日中に必ず撮りきってください。
examples.trans: In return, make sure you finish shooting everything before the day ends.

examples.text: 全部買ってやる。その代わりあんたの知恵をよこせ。
examples.trans: I will buy all of them. In exchange, give me your strategic brains.

meanings.note: Negates verbs or forms じゃない ('is not') in questions like いいんじゃないか.

examples.text: きっと情熱的な撮影をしてるんでしょうね、村西監督は。
examples.trans: Director Muranishi must be in the middle of a passionate shoot right now.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Checks agreement ('isn't it?') or softens a request or farewell.

examples.text: 昨日ね、お買い物してたら昔の同僚とたまたま会ったんです。
examples.trans: Yesterday while I was out shopping, I bumped into an old coworker by chance.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Attaches to a past-stem verb form to set up a condition ('if a fire starts').

examples.text: 火事になったら大変です。
examples.trans: If a fire breaks out, it will be terrible.

examples.text: 家に帰ったら電話します。
examples.trans: I will call when I get home.

examples.text: 昨日ね、お買い物してたら昔の同僚とたまたま会ったんです。
examples.trans: Yesterday while I was out shopping, I bumped into an old coworker by chance.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Polite volitional 会いましょう in また会いましょう means 'let us meet again'.

examples.trans: I meet a friend at the station.

examples.text: また来週会いましょう。
デパートで美容部員やってたんだって。センスいいのよ。
examples.trans: I heard she worked at a department store beauty counter. She has great taste.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: in that way; that is so
meanings.note: そうですか ('Is that so? / I see') calmly acknowledges news.

examples.text: そうですか、わかりました。

meanings.en: that (near the listener or just mentioned)
meanings.note: Must always precede a noun (その椅子 'that chair').
Standard gender-neutral 'I' in polite and business Japanese.
Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

meanings.note: Refers to facts, matters, or affairs rather than physical objects (もの).

examples.text: 仕事のことを話します。

meanings.en: know; find out; be aware of
meanings.note: Godan verb; state of knowing is 知っている.

examples.text: 彼の電話番号を知っていますか。
examples.trans: Do you know his phone number?

examples.text: 本当の理由を知りたい。
examples.trans: I want to know the real reason.

meanings.note: Read なん before だ/です/の, and なに before が/を or alone.

examples.text: 何を買いにきましたか。
examples.trans: What did you come to buy?

meanings.note: Written を and pronounced o; marks what an action directly acts upon.
Attaches to the irrealis (a-stem) of godan verbs.

examples.trans: I was called by the teacher.

meanings.note: Marks the presence of a person (責任者はいるか) or follows て-form (often contracted to てる/てます in speech).
Polite sentence-ending counterpart of plain だ.

cells: ではありません / じゃありません

meanings.note: Adverb.

examples.text: まだ終わっていません。

meanings.en: to think; to feel; to believe
meanings.note: Often follows quotative と to express an opinion or belief.

examples.text: それはいいと思います。

meanings.note: Follows a clause to give a reason or reassuring explanation.

examples.trans: Because it is close, I walk.

meanings.note: Ichidan verb: blunt imperative 見ろ ('look!') is rough command speech.

examples.text: これからガンガン稼いで、一緒にいい景色見るんだろうがよ！
examples.trans: We were going to earn big and see the view from the top together!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Plain sentence-ending copula; contracts or shifts to だった in past, だろう/だろ for supposition, and で/じゃ in combinations.

examples.text: 電車から見てた色のない景色とか、同じ予定だらけの手帳とか。
examples.trans: The colorless scenery from the commuter train, and a planner filled with the same routine...

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: open a store; bring out; hand in
meanings.note: 店を出す means opening a branch; 出しやがって attaches tough-guy disdainful やがる.

examples.text: 駅前に新しい店を出します。
examples.trans: We open a new branch in front of the station.

examples.text: 書類を出してください。

meanings.note: Expresses change of state, or in polite customer service (になります) states an arrangement or price total.

examples.trans: That comes to one thousand yen.

examples.text: お前ら、観光じゃないんだからしっかりしろよ。
examples.trans: Hey, this isn't sightseeing, so pull yourselves together.

examples.text: 彼女は来るんだろうな？
ちゃんとキャストはそろってるんだろうな？
examples.trans: You've got the whole cast properly lined up, right?

meanings.note: Indefinite pronoun.

examples.text: 分からないことがあれば何でも聞いてください。
examples.trans: If there's anything you don't understand, ask anything.

examples.text: 彼は料理なら何でも作れる。
examples.trans: He can make anything when it comes to cooking.

meanings.note: Irregular i-adjective whose past/conditional stems use よ- (よかったら).

examples.text: よかったら来てください。

meanings.note: Turns a statement into a question, or softens a volitional/negative guess.
Can stand at the head of a sentence without a particle ('right now').

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.
Used in everyday farewells like またね, また明日, and また会いましょう.

examples.text: また明日会いましょう。
